text:
maya: CI just turned red on master — warmup shard failing on L4s. Seeing both OOM and `invalid device function` in the same run. cc @sam @liam

sam: which job? link?

maya: https://ci.internal.redwood/graders/38291 — job: warmup-x86-l4-shard-7 (repro rate ~1/5)

ci-bot: Job 38291 failed on shard 7 — exit code 137. Logs uploaded: https://ci.internal.redwood/logs/38291/shard7

liam: quick skim — two notable things: driver on the L4 pool was upgraded yesterday to 545.23, but the docker image uses CUDA 11.8 runtime. `invalid device function` often means PTX vs SASS mismatch; OOM could be noise from failed kernel.

nina: I spun up l4-01 with the same image (redwood/inference-ci:cuda11.8-2026-03-11) and ran the warmup harness 10x. Hit same failure twice. From container dmesg:
```
[ 1234.56789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Ch 00000010, MMU fault, reason: PTE fetch, faulted address: 0x7f8c3d000000
[ 1234.56790] my_test_binary: cudaDriverGetVersion returned 9999
[ 1234.56791] my_test_binary: invalid device function
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```

maya: interesting, driver reports weird version 9999 in logs — suggests host driver/runtime mismatch or an NVML/driver mishandling.

sam: can you try setting CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY and rerun one warmup? sometimes JIT/warmup timing triggers this on newer drivers.

nina: reran with `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY ./run_warmup.sh --shard 7` — one run completed, one failed. Still flaky.

liam: next step: targeted rerun across two different node pools (old-driver and new-driver). If failure only on new-driver pool, we have a clear correlation. I'll queue 20 iterations on both. Command I used: `./tools/ci/targeted_rerun.sh --job warmup --shards 7 --nodes l4-pool-new,l4-pool-old --iters 20`

ci-bot: Queued targeted rerun (TG-7742). Results will post here when jobs finish.

maya: if reruns confirm driver correlation, we should pin the Dedicated canary image to the older driver and open a driver-rollout ticket for ops. Also add a short smoke that exercises tiny kernels to catch invalid-device-function before merge.

sam: agree. For short-term mitigation, nina — can you add MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 and `TORCH_USE_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` to the warmup wrapper to reduce fragmentation, in case OOM is amplifying the issue?

nina: done — created a small PR with the env changes to the warmup harness. If CI passes with env vars, we'll keep them for a week while ops investigates.

liam: if we need to bisect driver packages, ops has driver package snapshots from the last 10 days. Plan: binary search between driver 535.30 (last known good) and 545.23 (current). Ops, please hold a snapshot of 535.30 and 540.x for quick rollback.

maya: tagging product/infra slack channels so infra ops can prioritize: @ops-team please help pin drivers and preserve the old images.

sam: quick triage notes for the ticket: potential causes: (1) driver/runtime ABI mismatch (PTX/SASS), (2) JIT timing/regression on new driver, (3) memory fragmentation causing bad allocations after kernel failure. Steps taken: targeted reruns queued, local repro on l4-01, env mitigations PR, asking ops for driver pin + snapshots.

ci-bot: Targeted rerun TG-7742 finished: 40 runs total — failures: 6 on new-driver pool, 0 on old-driver pool.

maya: OK that pretty much nails it to the driver bump. Opening infra-ticket INFRA-1283 to pin drivers and schedule a rollout rollback. Thanks everyone — will follow up with rollback window once ops confirms snapshots. :thumbsup:
